metadata.title: Sugar #11 — El Niño + Hormuz Compound Thesis
metadata.subtitle: Feb'27 SB calls: 18¢ ×2 (May 22) + 19.5¢ ×1 (Aug 12) — compound thesis

thesis.headline: El Niño forecast strengthened again (NOAA Aug: 95% very strong, up from 81% in July) while NY sugar pushed to a fresh 15-month high on tightening deficit forecasts — India's nil-duty import quota still the swing factor into Oct 31.
thesis.summary: Two legs moved this week. El Niño: NOAA's mid-August update raised the odds of a very-strong Oct-Dec peak to 95% (from 81% in July), with a 69% chance the RONI index tops +2.5°C — which would exceed every El Niño since 1950. That's a further upgrade on top of an already-active Advisory, not a weakening. Price: NY #11 posted a 15-month high and London a 17-month high this week on the same deficit-tightening logic that's been building since Green Pool (-3.3 MMT) and StoneX (-1.7 MMT) revised deeper into deficit in late July. India's domestic retail prices are still climbing (~40% MoM by some counts) despite the Aug 20 nil-duty import quota, which is fueling political pushback at home even as it pulls ~1 MMT of new demand onto the world market. Brazil leg unchanged from last week: C-S 2H-July crush -8.4% YoY, sugar output -17.6%, ethanol mandate 32% — full 2026/27-season USDA estimates still peg the sugar/ethanol mix around 48/52%, well below the ~50/50 split of a year ago. Next question is unchanged: is 1 MMT of Indian imports enough, or does the quota get extended/enlarged after Oct 31.

elNino.probabilityWindow: El Niño Advisory ACTIVE (NOAA CPC, Aug 2026) — event formed and intensifying
elNino.strongEventOdds: 95% very strong (Niño 3.4/RONI ≥ +2.0°C) — up from 81% in July's CPC assessment; 69% chance RONI reaches +2.5°C+, which would exceed every El Niño on record since 1950
elNino.soiNote: NOAA's Aug RONI forecast puts the median Oct-Dec value at +2.66°C (middle 50% range +2.37 to +2.95°C); little indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027

millMix.brazilOutputNote: 2026/27 through May: sugar mix collapsed to 41.4% (from 50.1% a year ago) as mills pivot to ethanol — C-S sugar output 6.84 MMT, -2.0% YoY. This is the 'mill mix shift' leg of the tail scenario actually happening. 2H-July update: crush -8.4% YoY, sugar output -17.6% YoY, with the ethanol blend mandate raised to 32%. USDA's full-season 2026/27 Sugar Annual still projects the mix averaging closer to 48% sugar / 52% ethanol for the year — meaning the mid-year prints (41.4%, -17.6%) are running well below even that already-bearish full-season forecast. Exact first-half-August UNICA crush/mix figures were not obtainable this week (carried forward); processing volumes were reported 'up' in early August without a specific mix percentage.

exitTriggers.name: El Niño weakens / fails
exitTriggers.rationale: Was the primary risk — now essentially retired: NOAA's Aug update raised the odds of a very-strong Oct-Dec peak to 95% (from 81% in July), with a 69% chance of exceeding every El Niño on record since 1950. Persistence holds at 97% through early spring 2027. Residual risk is now just a peak that undershoots this already-elevated forecast, not a failure of the event itself.

exitTriggers.name: Hormuz ceasefire IV crush
exitTriggers.rationale: Options re-price down even before underlying moves. Pre-expiry risk.

exitTriggers.name: Brazilian mill mix stays at sugar
exitTriggers.rationale: Largely retired — mills have pivoted hard to ethanol: 2H-July crush -8.4% YoY, sugar output -17.6% YoY, with the ethanol blend mandate raised to 32%. Residual risk is a mix reversal if ethanol parity flips.

exitTriggers.name: India ethanol policy reversal
exitTriggers.rationale: Govt raises diversion → removes export supply (bullish risk for sugar but kills bear setup).

exitTriggers.name: Theta decay without move
exitTriggers.rationale: ~$3-5/day per OTM call. Manageable but compounds if no move by Q4.

tailScenario.title: Energy Lockdown → Sugar Deficit

components.mechanism: Brazilian mill mix shift to ethanol

tailScenario.context: 2024/25 deficit was 3.5 MMT → drove sugar +100% to 28¢. Lockdown deficit could be 2-3x larger.
tailScenario.inelasticDemandNote: Sugar is staple food. COVID: consumption fell 3-5%, recovered fast. 1973-74 energy crisis: consumption fell <10%, prices rose 6x.
